items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: me and my wife met him and his wife Lucille quite often whenever they came to Paris.

ctx.x: The death of Louis Armstrong on the 6th of July, 1971, two days after his 71st birthday(which was on July the 4th) was quite a shock to me and my wife, because Pops seemed to have been well on the way of recovering good health. I suppose that his sudden death was quite a surprise to most of the jazz world. I did not cry when I heard the sad news, as some people may have done, but my heart was heavy as lead. I admired Pop's way of playing when I heard his first record. The one I heard was when he was with Fletcher…

And when I got to know him as well as I did, and listened to so much of his horn playing, my admiration of him grew more and more. I am proud to say that I got to know him so well that me and my wife met him and his wife Lucille quite often whenever they came to Paris.

Louis, who was also known as Gate-Mouth, then Satchel-Mouth, which was shortened to Gate, Satchmo and was also called Pops, was a genius. He gave much to the jazz world with his original style of trumpet playing and jazz singing. There has been quite a few geniuses in jazz music after Satchmo, but many of them died young. But the world was fortunate to have had it's Louis, Pops, Gatemouth, Satchmo Armstrong for so many happy trumpet and singing years! He did so very much for jazz and to bring joys to the world of…
